theorems_inventory.statement: [Bounded Pixel-Space Non-Reconstructability] Under adversary constraints $A_0$ through $A_3$ and foundational assumptions ($A_{HW}, A_{PHYS}, A_{SPEC}$), pixel-space reconstruction from post-boundary representations is architecturally underdetermined and mathematically non-unique.

[Probabilistic Noninterference] If the abstraction function is many-to-one over identity space and no stochastic process is conditioned on raw frame entropy, then the framework satisfies probabilistic noninterference under adversaries $A_0$ through $A_3$.

[Bounded Temporal Exposure] Raw biometric data exposure to an active $A_3$ (Root) adversary intercepting live memory via OS-level debuggers is strictly bounded by the configured TTL parameter $\Delta$ (e.g., $\Delta \le 33$ms).

[Governance Token Non-Bypass] Under attacker classes $A_0$ through $A_3$, no post-boundary payload can be emitted to an external sink without the inclusion of a governance approval token evaluated and validated by a TCB-resident module.

[Fail-Closed State Reachability] Under non-kernel operational failure conditions (Process Crash, Network Partition, OOM, Power Loss), the system deterministically reaches a secure HALT or DEGRADED state where all privacy invariants are preserved.
